bluesky.text: People who have no contact with coders seem to have no idea how much an entire profession transformed in less than a year due to AI. It is so weird to still see comments here that AI hasn’t changed anything or that AI code is bad or that companies are retreating from AI use. Does not match reality.
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text:
In one of my favorite experiments, I told Fable 5.2 to build an endless, hands-off journey through 3D worlds linked by portals. 

25,000 agents created over 450 worlds inspired by books, art, places, all in code.

Play (its neat): portals-endless-worlds.netlify.app
Github: github.com/emollick/ai-...
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text:
In a little over a week we will see the release of The Last Human Game.

There will never be another AAA game at the scale of GTA 6 with no AI assistance. People in the future will look back at an all-human game with an billion dollar budget and wonder how they did it, like the Pyramids.
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text: 🚨 Our Generative AI Lab is releasing Primer: an open source agent-driven system where a teacher talks through lessons & gets back a playable simulation for their students, grounded in pedagogy. We hope educators & researchers build on it. Paper/prompts/code are open: gail.wharton.upenn.edu/primer/
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text:
Researcher Will Depue discovered that 4 top Chinese labs’ models were all trained on Blackwell GPUs (GB200 & GB300), which are fully restricted from sale to China

his method is purely forensic, no insider information was used

unemploymentlabs.com/checkpoint-f...
bluesky.author: mr. TIM

bluesky.text: The traffic from agent swarms doing research is going to be quite large, they are relentless at finding info. I had Fable 5.2 reconstruct WH Auden's 1941 poetry class. It found an obscure, relevant book on the Internet Archive, which it read a line at a time by doing repeated full text searches.
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text: Got to see student presentations today at the Generative AI Studio at Penn. It was a visceral way to feel how far creative people can now get using AI. Already, almost every project from an individual was 10x further along than a fully done team project from three years ago.
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text:
Had early access to Gemini 4 Carbon, it is a very good model that improves on Argon. It is useful to have an AI that thinks differently than Claude/GPT & is still highly capable, but has its own strengths & weakness

One fun demo: I gave Carbon a video clip & it reproduced it in 3js very well
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text:
great take 

every “crisis” around AI has been a latent problem for years, and was causing problems before, just unignorable now
bluesky.author: mr. TIM

bluesky.text:
AI is getting better faster than our measurements are.

I threw together SatBench, which measures how quickly major AI benchmarks become saturated (effectively solved) by AI. Of 173 benchmarks cited by the Labs since 2023, 63% are now saturated. Saturation of new benchmarks is also happening faster.
bluesky.author: Ethan Mollick

bluesky.text: Looks like Fable 5.2 is above the already steep trendline on three of the most informative unsaturated benchmarks (ECI is a composite of other benchmarks, Remote Labor measures the ability to do end-to-end freelance jobs, RoboDojo involves controlling robotics).
